summary: No held thesis is broken by evidence in the files. There were no fills on 11-18. All twelve single-name holdings (DPZ, CARG, VRSN, SAM, IDXX, EXEL, INCY, KR, MSCI, FAST, WMT, MCO) are still on the 11-17 menu with fscore_computable 9, CFO above net income and empty flags, so every 'screen drops it from the menu' and 'CFO below net income' clause is untripped. The book ended at $621.35 (+3.56% since inception against SPY -4.73%, -0.19% since v6 against SPY -2.63%). The day's risk sits in price stops and one event, not in the fundamentals: SPY is 0.06% above the shared VOO/VTI line (730.2 vs 729.79), MCO is 2.4% above its $470 stop, and WMT reports 11-19. No lesson in learning.json names the fundamentals analyst, and I have no graded calls. I applied L3's label caveat because it bears on how the screen data is read.
update: Holding-by-holding check against the menu (untripped unless stated). MCO: on the menu at gp_sector_pct 0.825, F8, CFO $2.90B vs NI $2.46B. Of all holdings it has the lowest in-sector percentile, close to the 0.80 top-20% cutoff, so it is the held name most likely to drop off on a screen rebuild. It fails leverage_not_up, as MSCI (0.903, CFO $1.59B vs NI $1.20B) does, which is a concern for the whole financial-data sleeve. Its screen 'Industrials' label is the same SIC artifact as MSCI's. The PM's 'first sell candidate' framing rests on the Market Analyst and the stop, not on the fundamentals, which have not changed. SAM: on the menu (0.945, F8, CFO $270M vs NI $108M, mark $223.48 vs fill $220.14). The data is FY2025 (fy_end 2025-12-27), so it says nothing about 2026 trading. EXEL: on the menu (0.934, F7, CFO $884M vs NI $783M), 5.1% above $65. F7 is the screen floor, and EXEL fails gross_margin_improved and current_ratio_improved. INCY: on the menu (0.905, F8). No new filing, and MAESTRA-3 was already judged. WMT: on the menu (0.863, F7 at the floor, CFO $41.6B vs NI $21.9B, fy_end 2026-01-31). The 11-19 print is a 10-Q, so it cannot change these 10-K-based numbers. Only the guidance-cut clause and the $119 stop can trip, and a close-based stop does not protect against a gap. KR: on the menu (0.890, F7 at the floor, CFO $7.31B vs NI $1.02B). The cyber clause is unconfirmed, and Stifel's $80 initiation is supportive but is not a fundamentals datum. DPZ: on the menu (1.0, F8, CFO $792M vs NI $602M, fails leverage_not_up). Its Staples rank is still the wholesale-groceries SIC artifact. CARG: on the menu (1.0, F8, CFO $295M vs NI $156M). Its vol_252d of 0.406 is the closest of any holding to the 0.443 volatility cutoff, and vol moves daily, so CARG is the held name most likely to drop off for a non-fundamental reason. If it does, review it under the menu-drop rule rather than selling it automatically. VRSN (F9, 0.993), IDXX (0.942, F8), FAST (0.873, F8, CFO only slightly above NI at $1.296B vs $1.258B, Consumer Discretionary label though Industrials by business) and MSCI: no change. VOO/VTI are ETFs and outside the screen (holdings_not_on_menu), so they have no fundamentals thesis to break. Their SPY 200-day stop is the Market Analyst's and PM's call. For the next morning: (1) re-check the menu clause for MCO, EXEL and SAM, the holdings whose theses name it; (2) after WMT's 11-19 print, judge only the guidance clause, since the screen data will not move until the FY2027 10-K; (3) keep treating MCO and MSCI as one sleeve that shares the leverage_not_up failure.
